name: nifty_intraday_momentum_factor_v1
author: quant_system
thesis: Cross-sectional intraday momentum: stocks that outperformed in the first 90 minutes continue to outperform for the next 90 minutes, and vice versa. This is driven by institutional order-splitting — a large buy order in the morning continues executing through the afternoon. The inefficiency exists because cross-sectional sorting requires real-time ranking of 50 stocks, which most retail platforms can't do. Not fully arbitraged because the edge is thin per-trade and requires trading multiple names simultaneously.
stock_filter: all 50 NIFTY constituents, rank by morning return

long.confirmation: rank computed at 10:45, enter at market

short.confirmation: rank computed at 10:45, enter at market

exit.signal_exit: N/A — hold until time stop or profit/stop

filters.event_filter: skip stocks with earnings today, skip budget/RBI days entirely
other_filters: minimum 0.3% absolute morning return to qualify for top/bottom
skip if morning return is driven by single large gap (open price outlier)

edge.edge_decay_risk: medium — structural (institutional order flow) but studied in literature

weaknesses: 10 simultaneous positions at Zerodha = ₹400+ brokerage per day. Need consistent edge to justify the fixed cost overhead.
Morning momentum can reverse at exactly the entry time (10:45) due to profit-taking. The 90-min lookback is arbitrary.
Long/short construction is imperfect — NIFTY 50 is not truly market-neutral when you're long top 5 and short bottom 5. Sector concentration risk.
prior_art: Intraday cross-sectional momentum. Academic: Gao et al. (2018) on intraday momentum patterns. Also: Jegadeesh/Titman adapted to intraday.
notes: Capital-intensive. Needs ₹10L+ allocation. Not suitable for small accounts.
